question:
Which of the following statements is true with respect to the Maritime Anti-Piracy Act, 2022?

1) Parliament gave its approval to the Maritime Anti-Piracy Bill, 2022 in the Rajya Sabha in December 2022.

2) The Act enables Indian authorities to take action against piracy on the high seas.

3) It applies to the sea beyond the Exclusive Economic Zone, which is above 500 nautical miles from the coast of India.

4) The Act defines piracy as any illegal act of violence, detention or destruction against a ship, aircraft or person, committed for private purposes by the crew or passengers of a private ship or aircraft.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1, 2 and 4.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Maritime Anti-Piracy Act, 2022 was passed by the Lok Sabha in December 2021 and cleared by the Rajya Sabha in December 2022, thus completing Parliament's approval in December 2022 — so statement 1 is correct.

• The Act empowers Indian authorities (the Navy and the Coast Guard) to act against piracy on the high seas, and provides for the prosecution of pirates in Indian courts — so statement 2 is correct.

• The Act defines piracy as any illegal act of violence, detention or destruction committed for private ends by the crew or passengers of a private ship or aircraft against another ship, aircraft, person or property — so statement 4 is correct.

• Statement 3 is WRONG. The Act applies to the sea beyond the Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ), i.e., beyond 200 nautical miles from India's coastline — not 500 nautical miles.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Act gives effect to India's obligations under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), 1982, which India ratified in 1995.

• Punishment under the Act: life imprisonment for piracy; death penalty where the act of piracy causes or attempts to cause death.

• Maritime zones of India: Territorial Waters – 12 nautical miles, Contiguous Zone – 24 nm, Exclusive Economic Zone – 200 nm, beyond which lie the high seas.

NOTE

• Piracy has been a serious problem off the Gulf of Aden and the Somali coast; the Indian Navy has conducted sustained anti-piracy patrols there since 2008.

question: How long can a person remain a minister without being a member of either House of the State Legislature?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 6 months.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under Article 164(4) of the Constitution of India, a Minister of a State who is not a member of either House of the State Legislature for a period of six consecutive months ceases to be a Minister at the end of that period. (छह माह)

• In other words, such a minister must get elected (or nominated) to the State Legislature within six months, failing which the office is automatically vacated.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The parallel provision for the Union Council of Ministers is Article 75(5), which lays down the same six-month rule for a Union Minister who is not a member of either House of Parliament.

• Article 163 — Council of Ministers to aid and advise the Governor.

• Article 164(1) — The Chief Minister is appointed by the Governor; other ministers are appointed by the Governor on the advice of the Chief Minister.

• Article 164(2) — The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly of the State.

NOTE

• Article 164(1A) (inserted by the 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003) caps the size of the State Council of Ministers at 15% of the total strength of the Legislative Assembly, subject to a minimum of 12 ministers.

question: The world's largest camel fair is held in which of the following cities?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pushkar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Pushkar Camel Fair (Pushkar Mela), held at Pushkar in Ajmer district, Rajasthan, is regarded as the world's largest camel fair. (पुष्कर पशु मेला)

• It is held annually in the Hindu month of Kartik (October–November), culminating on Kartik Purnima, and combines a huge livestock market with religious bathing in the sacred Pushkar Lake.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Pushkar is famous for the only major temple of Lord Brahma in India.

• Bikaner hosts the well-known Camel Festival in January, and also houses the National Research Centre on Camel.

• Other famous fairs of Rajasthan: Nagaur Cattle Fair (second largest in India), Teej Fair (Jaipur), Gangaur Fair, Urs Fair (Ajmer), Baneshwar Fair (Dungarpur).

NOTE

• The camel is the state animal of Rajasthan. Camel breeds of the region include Bikaneri, Jaisalmeri, Marwari, Mewari and Kachchhi.

question: Who among the following Indian musicians is the inventor of Mohan Veena?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pandit Vishwa Mohan Bhatt.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pandit Vishwa Mohan Bhatt created the Mohan Veena by modifying an archtop Hawaiian/slide guitar — adding extra melody, drone and sympathetic strings (a total of about 19–20 strings) so that it could produce the full range of Hindustani classical ornamentation such as meend, gamak and jhala. (मोहन वीणा)

• He is a disciple of Pandit Ravi Shankar and belongs to the Maihar gharana.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Vishwa Mohan Bhatt won the Grammy Award (1994) for the album "A Meeting by the River" with the American guitarist Ry Cooder.

• He was awarded the Padma Shri (2002) and the Padma Bhushan (2017).

• Pandit Brij Bhushan Kabra was the pioneer who first adapted the guitar to Hindustani classical music, but the Mohan Veena as an instrument is credited to Vishwa Mohan Bhatt.

• Sandeep Das is a renowned tabla player and a Grammy winner with the Silk Road Ensemble.

NOTE

• Other modern Indian instrument innovations: Shankar's Double Violin, the Trichy Sankaran mridangam style, and the Sarod refinements of the Maihar gharana.

question: Mulk Raj Anand is the author of _____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Untouchable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mulk Raj Anand (1905–2004) wrote the classic Indian-English novel "Untouchable" (1935), which depicts a single day in the life of Bakha, a young sweeper, and exposes the cruelty of untouchability. (अछूत)

• Anand is regarded, along with R. K. Narayan and Raja Rao, as one of the founding trio of Indian writing in English.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Other works by Mulk Raj Anand: Coolie (1936), Two Leaves and a Bud (1937), The Village, Across the Black Waters, The Sword and the Sickle, The Big Heart, Private Life of an Indian Prince.

• "The Guide" (1958) was written by R. K. Narayan (Sahitya Akademi Award, 1960).

• "The Invisible Man" (1897) is a science-fiction novel by H. G. Wells.

• "A Passage to India" (1924) is by E. M. Forster.

NOTE

• Mulk Raj Anand received the Padma Bhushan in 1967 and the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1971 for "Morning Face".

question: Which of the following musicians of medieval India is referred to as 'Tuti-e-Hind' and is also regarded as the father of qawwali?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Amir Khusrau.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Amir Khusrau (1253–1325) is famously called "Tuti-e-Hind" — the Parrot of India — for his sweetness of expression, and is regarded as the father of qawwali. (तूती-ए-हिंद)

• He was a disciple of the Chishti Sufi saint Hazrat Nizamuddin Auliya and served in the courts of several Delhi Sultans, including Alauddin Khalji.

• He is credited by tradition with developing the sitar and the tabla, and with creating the Khayal style and many ragas such as Yaman, Zeelaf and Sarparda.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Literary works of Amir Khusrau: Khazain-ul-Futuh, Tughlaq Nama, Nuh Sipihr, Qiran-us-Sadain, Miftah-ul-Futuh, Ashiqa.

• Miyan Tansen was one of the Navaratnas of Akbar's court and a disciple of Swami Haridas; ragas Miyan ki Malhar, Miyan ki Todi and Darbari Kanada are attributed to him.

• Purandara Dasa is called the "Pitamaha (father) of Carnatic music".

• Swami Haridas was a saint-musician of the Vrindavan tradition and the guru of Tansen.

NOTE

• Qawwali is a form of Sufi devotional music sung at dargahs; famous exponents include Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan and the Sabri Brothers.

question: The blue green alga Anabaena lives in the leaves of Azolla, a freshwater fern, forming which of the following relationships?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Symbiotic.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Anabaena azollae, a blue-green alga (cyanobacterium), lives inside the leaf cavities of the water fern Azolla in a symbiotic (mutually beneficial) relationship. (सहजीवी संबंध)

◦ Anabaena fixes atmospheric nitrogen through its specialised cells called heterocysts and supplies it to the fern.

◦ Azolla in turn provides the alga with shelter and carbon compounds (food).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Azolla–Anabaena association is widely used as a biofertiliser in paddy fields, especially in South-East Asia and India, because it enriches the soil with nitrogen.

• Autotrophic — organisms that prepare their own food (green plants, cyanobacteria).

• Parasitic — one organism benefits at the expense of the host (Cuscuta on other plants).

• Saprophytic — organisms feeding on dead and decaying matter (mushrooms, moulds).

NOTE

• Other important nitrogen-fixing associations: Rhizobium with the root nodules of legumes, Frankia with Casuarina, and the free-living fixers Azotobacter and Clostridium.

question: Who was famous for publishing a formula in 1827 that shows the mathematical relationship between current, resistance and voltage?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Georg Simon Ohm.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The German physicist Georg Simon Ohm published Ohm's Law in 1827 in his work "Die galvanische Kette, mathematisch bearbeitet". (ओम का नियम)

• Ohm's Law: at constant temperature, the current (I) flowing through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference (V) across it.

◦ V = I × R, where R is the resistance.

◦ Hence I = V/R and R = V/I.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The SI unit of resistance, the ohm (Ω), is named after him; its reciprocal, conductance, is measured in siemens (S) or mho.

• William Gilbert wrote "De Magnete" (1600) and is called the father of magnetism/electricity studies.

• Gustav Kirchhoff gave Kirchhoff's Current Law (junction rule) and Voltage Law (loop rule) for electrical circuits in 1845.

• William Watson was an 18th-century English scientist who worked on the conduction of electricity.

NOTE

• Resistance of a conductor: R = ρL/A, where ρ is resistivity, L is length and A is area of cross-section.

• Electric power: P = VI = I²R = V²/R. Commercial unit of energy: 1 kWh = 3.6 × 10⁶ joule.

question: Identify the correct pair (name of shifting agriculture and related state) from the following.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bewar – Madhya Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Shifting cultivation (slash-and-burn agriculture) is known by different local names in different parts of India. (झूम / स्थानांतरी कृषि)

◦ Bewar / Dahiya / Penda / Beera — Madhya Pradesh (Bundelkhand and Baghelkhand tribal belts). Hence Option 1 is the correct pair.

• In this system, a patch of forest is cleared and burnt, cropped for two or three years and then abandoned so that fertility can be restored naturally.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Kuruwa — Jharkhand (not Punjab).

• Podu / Penda — Andhra Pradesh and Odisha (not Tamil Nadu).

• Bringa — Odisha (not Uttar Pradesh).

• Other regional names: Jhum — North-Eastern states (Assam, Nagaland, Mizoram); Kumari — Western Ghats/Kerala; Khil — Uttarakhand/Himachal Pradesh; Valre or Waltre — south-eastern Rajasthan; Dipa — Bastar (Chhattisgarh) and the Andaman & Nicobar Islands; Zabo — Nagaland (a water-harvesting farming system).

NOTE

• Outside India: Milpa — Mexico and Central America; Ladang — Indonesia and Malaysia; Ray — Vietnam; Chena — Sri Lanka; Conuco — Venezuela; Roca — Brazil; Masole — Central Africa.

question: The Balti dance of ____________ is distinct as it has its own costume, music and songs in the Balti language. The dance is only performed on rare occasions, such as feasts or celebrations.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ladakh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Balti dance belongs to the Kargil region of Ladakh, home to the Balti people, and is performed in the Balti language with its own distinctive costume and music. (बाल्टी नृत्य — लद्दाख)

• It is performed only on special occasions such as feasts, weddings and celebrations, which is why it is rarely seen.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Other folk dances of Ladakh: Jabro, Shondol (recognised by the Guinness Book as the largest Ladakhi dance), Chham (mask dance of monasteries), Koshan, Spao-Kar-Tses (warrior dance).

• Folk dances of Jammu & Kashmir: Rouf, Hafiza, Bhand Pather, Dumhal, Kud, Bhangra (Jammu region).

• Folk dances of Himachal Pradesh: Nati (Guinness record for the largest folk dance), Losar Shona Chuksam, Kinnauri, Dangi.

• Folk dances of Uttarakhand: Langvir, Barada Nati, Chholiya, Jhora, Chhapeli.

NOTE

• Ladakh became a Union Territory (without a legislature) on 31 October 2019 after the reorganisation of the erstwhile State of Jammu & Kashmir. Its two districts are Leh and Kargil.

question: The Fundamental Duties of Indian Citizens were adopted from the Constitution of which country?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Soviet Union.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution were borrowed from the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR (Soviet Union). (मौलिक कर्तव्य — सोवियत संघ से)

• They were added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee, and are listed in Part IV-A, Article 51A.

• Originally 10 duties were added; an 11th duty — that every parent/guardian must provide education to a child between the ages of 6 and 14 years — was inserted by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other borrowings: Fundamental Rights, judicial review, impeachment of the President, removal of Supreme Court and High Court judges — USA; Parliamentary system, rule of law, single citizenship, writs — UK; Directive Principles of State Policy — Ireland; Concurrent List, freedom of trade and commerce — Australia; Emergency provisions — Germany (Weimar); Federal structure with a strong Centre and residuary powers — Canada; Procedure established by law — Japan; Amendment procedure — South Africa; Preamble's ideals of liberty, equality, fraternity — France.

NOTE

• Fundamental Duties, like the Directive Principles, are non-justiciable — they cannot be enforced by the courts — but they serve as constitutional reminders to citizens.

question: Which state hosted the 36th National Games of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gujarat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 36th National Games of India were held in Gujarat from 29 September to 12 October 2022, across six cities — Ahmedabad, Gandhinagar, Surat, Vadodara, Rajkot and Bhavnagar. (36वें राष्ट्रीय खेल — गुजरात)

• The Games were inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the Narendra Modi Stadium, Ahmedabad. The mascot was "Savaj" (an Asiatic lion cub).

• Services Sports Control Board (SSCB) topped the medal tally, followed by Maharashtra and Haryana.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The 37th National Games (2023) were hosted by Goa (25 October – 9 November 2023); Maharashtra topped that medal tally.

• The 35th National Games (2015) were held in Kerala.

• The National Games are organised under the aegis of the Indian Olympic Association (IOA).

NOTE

• Gujarat is also home to the Narendra Modi Stadium (Motera) in Ahmedabad — the world's largest cricket stadium with a capacity of about 1,32,000 spectators.

question: Jet streams are a particular form of:
solution_text:
The correct answer is geostrophic winds.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Jet streams are narrow bands of very fast-moving air in the upper troposphere/lower stratosphere, and they are a particular form of geostrophic winds. (भूविक्षेपी पवनें)

• Geostrophic winds are winds that blow parallel to the isobars because the pressure gradient force is exactly balanced by the Coriolis force; this balance occurs in the upper atmosphere where friction is absent.

• Jet stream speeds can reach 110–185 km/h (and even over 400 km/h in winter), and they blow generally from west to east.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Major jet streams: Polar Jet Stream, Subtropical Westerly Jet Stream, Tropical Easterly Jet Stream and the Somali Jet.

• The Subtropical Westerly Jet blows south of the Himalayas in winter; its northward shift in summer is linked to the onset of the South-West Monsoon in India.

• The Tropical Easterly Jet (over peninsular India in summer) helps in the advance of the monsoon.

• Weather fronts are boundaries between two air masses of different temperature and humidity (warm, cold, stationary and occluded fronts).

NOTE

• Winds classification: Planetary/Permanent winds (trade, westerlies, polar easterlies), Periodic/Seasonal winds (monsoon, land and sea breeze), Local winds (Loo, Chinook, Foehn, Mistral, Sirocco).

question: According to the Global Multidimensional Poverty Index Report 2022, a total of 415 million people exited multidimensional poverty in India in the last ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 15 years.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Global Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) Report 2022, released jointly by the UNDP and the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI), reported that 415 million people in India exited multidimensional poverty within 15 years (between 2005–06 and 2019–21). (15 वर्ष)

• India's MPI poverty headcount fell from about 55.1% in 2005–06 to 16.4% in 2019–21.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Global MPI measures poverty across three dimensions and ten indicators:

◦ Health — nutrition, child mortality.

◦ Education — years of schooling, school attendance.

◦ Standard of living — cooking fuel, sanitation, drinking water, electricity, housing, assets.

• A person is identified as multidimensionally poor if he/she is deprived in at least one-third (33.3%) of the weighted indicators.

• NITI Aayog releases India's own National Multidimensional Poverty Index, which adds two indicators — maternal health and bank account — making 12 indicators.

NOTE

• The MPI concept is based on the Alkire–Foster method developed at OPHI, University of Oxford. It has been published in the UNDP Human Development Report since 2010.

question: What is the primary function of a commercial bank?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Granting loans and accepting deposits.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The primary (main) functions of a commercial bank are:

◦ Accepting deposits — savings, current, fixed and recurring deposits from the public.

◦ Granting loans and advances — term loans, cash credit, overdraft, discounting of bills.

• A commercial bank is essentially a financial intermediary: it mobilises the savings of surplus units and lends them to deficit units, earning the spread between the lending rate and the deposit rate. (वाणिज्यिक बैंक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1, 2 and 4 are the functions of the central bank (Reserve Bank of India):

◦ Issuing currency notes — the RBI issues all notes except the one-rupee note and coins, which are issued by the Ministry of Finance, Government of India.

◦ Conducting monetary policy and regulating the money supply through the repo rate, reverse repo rate, CRR, SLR and open market operations.

• Secondary functions of commercial banks: agency services (collection of cheques, payment of bills), general utility services (lockers, letters of credit, foreign exchange) and credit creation.

NOTE

• Credit creation is a unique function of commercial banks: total credit created = Primary deposits × (1/CRR), where 1/CRR is the credit multiplier.

• The RBI was established on 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act, 1934 and was nationalised on 1 January 1949.

question: Which of the following is an example of revenue receipt in the government budget?
option_2: Repayment of a loan by a state-owned company
option_3: Dividends received from a state-owned enterprise
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dividends received from a state-owned enterprise.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Revenue receipts are those receipts of the government which (i) do not create any liability and (ii) do not cause any reduction in the assets of the government. (राजस्व प्राप्तियाँ)

• Dividends and profits received from Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) satisfy both conditions — no liability is created and no asset is sold — so they are non-tax revenue receipts.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Why the other options are capital receipts:

◦ Sale of government-owned land (and disinvestment of PSU shares) reduces the assets of the government.

◦ Repayment of a loan by a state-owned company — recovery of loans reduces a financial asset of the government.

◦ Borrowing from international organisations creates a liability.

• Revenue receipts are of two kinds: tax revenue (income tax, corporation tax, GST, customs, excise) and non-tax revenue (interest receipts, dividends and profits, fees, fines, grants).

NOTE

• Revenue Deficit = Revenue Expenditure − Revenue Receipts.

• Fiscal Deficit = Total Expenditure − Total Receipts (excluding borrowings).

• Primary Deficit = Fiscal Deficit − Interest Payments.

question: Birsa Munda Hockey Stadium was built in which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odisha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Birsa Munda International Hockey Stadium is located in Rourkela, Sundargarh district, Odisha. (बिरसा मुंडा हॉकी स्टेडियम — ओडिशा)

• It was built for the FIH Men's Hockey World Cup 2023, which Odisha co-hosted along with the Kalinga Stadium, Bhubaneswar.

• With a seating capacity of about 20,000, it is the largest hockey stadium in India (and among the largest in the world) in terms of seating capacity.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• It is named after the tribal freedom fighter Birsa Munda (1875–1900), leader of the Ulgulan (Great Tumult) movement in the Chhotanagpur region, who is revered as "Dharti Aaba" (Father of the Earth). 15 November, his birth anniversary, is observed as Janjatiya Gaurav Divas.

• Sundargarh district is regarded as the cradle of Indian hockey; hockey stars Dilip Tirkey, Amit Rohidas and Birendra Lakra come from there.

• Odisha has been the official sponsor of the Indian men's and women's hockey teams since 2018.

NOTE

• India won the hockey bronze medal at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics (held in 2021) — its first Olympic hockey medal in 41 years — and again a bronze at Paris 2024.

question: Who received the title Pandita from the faculty of Calcutta University for her knowledge of Sanskrit?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ramabai Sarasvati.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pandita Ramabai Sarasvati (1858–1922) was honoured with the titles "Pandita" and "Saraswati" by the faculty (scholars) of Calcutta University in 1878 in recognition of her extraordinary command of Sanskrit — a rare distinction for a woman of that age. (पंडिता रमाबाई)

• She was a pioneering social reformer who worked for the education and rehabilitation of widows and destitute women.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Pandita Ramabai founded the Arya Mahila Samaj (1882) in Pune, the Sharada Sadan (1889) in Bombay and the Mukti Mission (1896) at Kedgaon near Pune.

• Her famous book "The High-Caste Hindu Woman" (1887) exposed the oppression of women in Indian society.

• Rokeya Sakhawat Hossain wrote the feminist utopian story "Sultana's Dream" (1905) and founded a school for Muslim girls in Kolkata.

• Sarojini Naidu, the "Nightingale of India", was the first Indian woman President of the Indian National Congress (Kanpur, 1925) and the first woman Governor of an Indian state (United Provinces).

• Rassundari Devi wrote "Amar Jiban" (1876), the first full-fledged autobiography in Bengali and the first by an Indian woman.

NOTE

• The British government awarded her the Kaisar-i-Hind medal in 1919 for her social service.

question: Rani Machaiah from Karnataka was awarded the Padma Shri for her contribution to popularising ___________ in and outside Karnataka.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ummathat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rani Machaiah of Kodagu (Coorg), Karnataka received the Padma Shri in 2023 for popularising the Ummathat (Umathat) dance — a traditional folk dance of the Kodava community performed by women. (उम्मत्ताट नृत्य)

• In Ummathat, women dressed in traditional Kodava red silk saris dance in a circle, clapping and singing, usually during the Kaveri Sankramana and Huthri (harvest) festivals.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Kamsale Nritya — a vigorous folk dance of the devotees of Lord Mahadeshwara in the Mysuru–Chamarajanagar region, performed with brass cymbal-like discs.

• Kunitha — a group of ritual folk dances of Karnataka, including Dollu Kunitha (drum dance), Pooja Kunitha and Veeragase.

• Karadi Majalu — a folk percussion ensemble/dance of coastal Karnataka.

• Other classic Karnataka folk arts: Yakshagana, Bayalata, Suggi Kunitha, Somana Kunitha.

NOTE

• The Padma Awards — Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan and Padma Shri — are announced on the eve of Republic Day every year and conferred by the President of India.

question: Shri Domar Singh Kunvar from Chhattisgarh was honoured with ________ in the year 2023 for his contribution to 'Natya Nach'.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Padma Shri.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Shri Domar Singh Kunvar of Chhattisgarh was conferred the Padma Shri in 2023 in the field of Art for his lifelong contribution to "Natya Nach" — the traditional Nacha folk theatre of Chhattisgarh. (पद्म श्री)

• Nacha is a popular folk-theatre form of Chhattisgarh that combines dance, music, satire and social commentary, usually performed through the night in villages.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Order of precedence of the Padma Awards: Padma Vibhushan (exceptional and distinguished service) > Padma Bhushan (distinguished service of a high order) > Padma Shri (distinguished service in any field).

• The Bharat Ratna is the highest civilian award of India, instituted in 1954; it is not restricted to any field of activity.

• Padma Awards are given in the disciplines of Art, Social Work, Public Affairs, Science and Engineering, Trade and Industry, Medicine, Literature and Education, Sports, and Civil Service.

NOTE

• Other well-known folk theatre forms: Nautanki (Uttar Pradesh), Tamasha (Maharashtra), Bhavai (Gujarat), Jatra (West Bengal), Swang (Haryana), Pandavani (Chhattisgarh — popularised by Padma Vibhushan Teejan Bai).

question: Which of the following hills are located in Purvachal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mizo hills and Naga hills.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Purvachal (Eastern Hills or Purvanchal) is the eastern extension of the Himalayas, running along India's north-eastern border after the Himalayas take a sharp southward bend at the Dihang (Brahmaputra) gorge. (पूर्वांचल की पहाड़ियाँ)

• From north to south, the Purvachal comprises the Patkai Bum, Naga Hills, Manipur Hills and the Mizo (Lushai) Hills. Hence Option 1 is correct.

• These hills are composed largely of soft, unconsolidated sedimentary rocks and are covered with dense forests.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Shevroy and Javadi hills are outliers of the Eastern Ghats in Tamil Nadu.

• Khasi, Garo and Jaintia hills form the Meghalaya (Shillong) Plateau, which is a detached part of the Peninsular Plateau, not of the Purvachal.

• Anai Mudi (2,695 m) — the highest peak of peninsular India, in the Western Ghats (Kerala) — and Doda Betta (2,637 m) — the highest peak of the Nilgiris — belong to the Western Ghats.

NOTE

• The highest peak of the Purvachal region is Saramati (3,826 m) in Nagaland.

• Mawsynram and Cherrapunji (Sohra) in the Khasi Hills of Meghalaya record among the highest rainfall in the world.

question: The mausoleum of the Taj Mahal was designed by _______________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ustad Ahmad Lahori.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The mausoleum of the Taj Mahal at Agra is credited to the chief architect Ustad Ahmad Lahori (also known as Ustad Ahmad Lahauri). (उस्ताद अहमद लाहौरी)

• The Taj Mahal was built by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan between 1632 and 1653 in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal (Arjumand Banu Begum), on the right bank of the Yamuna.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Taj Mahal is built of white Makrana marble (from Rajasthan) and is famous for its pietra dura (parchin kari) inlay work with semi-precious stones.

• It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983 and is one of the New Seven Wonders of the World (2007).

• Other Mughal monuments: Red Fort and Jama Masjid, Delhi (Shah Jahan), Humayun's Tomb (designed by Mirak Mirza Ghiyas, built by Hamida Banu Begum), Buland Darwaza and Fatehpur Sikri (Akbar), Itmad-ud-Daulah's Tomb (Nur Jahan — called the "Baby Taj").

NOTE

• The Taj Mahal is a classic example of the charbagh (four-quartered garden) layout, and its perfect symmetry is broken only by the later-added cenotaph of Shah Jahan himself.

question: What was the Swadeshi Movement called in the state of Andhra Pradesh?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vande Mataram Movement.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the Andhra region (then part of the Madras Presidency), the Swadeshi Movement (1905–08) came to be popularly known as the "Vande Mataram Movement". (वंदे मातरम् आंदोलन)

• The movement was launched in reaction to the Partition of Bengal announced by Lord Curzon in 1905 (effective 16 October 1905), and it spread across India under different local names.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Swadeshi/Boycott movement was led in Bengal by Surendranath Banerjea, Bipin Chandra Pal and Aurobindo Ghosh; in Punjab by Lala Lajpat Rai; in Maharashtra by Bal Gangadhar Tilak; in Madras by Chidambaram Pillai; and in Delhi by Syed Haider Raza.

• "Vande Mataram" was composed by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay and appears in his novel "Anandamath" (1882). It was first sung at the 1896 Calcutta session of the Congress by Rabindranath Tagore and was adopted as the National Song on 24 January 1950.

• The Ghadar Movement (1913) was founded in the USA by Lala Har Dayal and Sohan Singh Bhakna.

• The Khilafat Movement (1919–24) was led by the Ali brothers (Maulana Muhammad Ali and Shaukat Ali).

• The Quit India Movement began on 8 August 1942 with Gandhiji's call of "Do or Die".

NOTE

• The Partition of Bengal was annulled in 1911 at the Delhi Durbar, when the capital was also shifted from Calcutta to Delhi.

question: 'Midnight's Children' is a novel by which of the following writers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Salman Rushdie.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Midnight's Children" (1981) is the celebrated novel by Sir Salman Rushdie. It tells the story of Saleem Sinai, born at the exact stroke of midnight on 15 August 1947, and uses magical realism to allegorise India's history after Independence. (मिडनाइट्स चिल्ड्रन)

• The novel won the Booker Prize (1981), and later the Booker of Bookers (1993) and the Best of the Booker (2008).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Other works by Salman Rushdie: Grimus, Shame, The Satanic Verses, The Moor's Last Sigh, The Ground Beneath Her Feet, Joseph Anton (memoir), Quichotte, Victory City.

• Jane Austen — Pride and Prejudice, Sense and Sensibility, Emma, Mansfield Park, Persuasion.

• Vikram Seth — A Suitable Boy, The Golden Gate, An Equal Music, Two Lives.

• Chetan Bhagat — Five Point Someone, One Night @ the Call Center, The 3 Mistakes of My Life, 2 States, Half Girlfriend.

NOTE

• Indian-origin Booker Prize winners: V. S. Naipaul (1971), Salman Rushdie (1981), Arundhati Roy (1997 — The God of Small Things), Kiran Desai (2006 — The Inheritance of Loss), Aravind Adiga (2008 — The White Tiger). Geetanjali Shree won the International Booker Prize (2022) for "Tomb of Sand (Ret Samadhi)".

question: Which of the following countries hosted the IBA Women's World Boxing Championships for the third time in March 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India hosted the IBA Women's World Boxing Championships for the third time in March 2023, at the Indira Gandhi Stadium Complex, New Delhi (15–26 March 2023). (भारत — तीसरी बार)

• India had earlier hosted the event in 2006 (New Delhi) and 2018 (New Delhi).

• India finished with 4 gold medals at the 2023 edition — won by Nikhat Zareen (50 kg), Nitu Ghanghas (48 kg), Lovlina Borgohain (75 kg) and Saweety Boora (81 kg) — and topped the medal tally.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The championship's mascot was "Veera", and the total prize money was US$ 2.4 million.

• MC Mary Kom holds the record of six gold medals at the Women's World Boxing Championships (2002, 2005, 2006, 2008, 2010 and 2018).

• The International Boxing Association (IBA) — formerly AIBA — is headquartered in Lausanne, Switzerland.

NOTE

• Nikhat Zareen became only the second Indian woman after Mary Kom to win two World Championship gold medals (2022 Istanbul and 2023 New Delhi).
